name: Gouged Block
desc: A block that is never finished — the gouge keeps scooping the lights away along the contours of a drifting form, the wood's own grain and knots printing through whatever ink is left, and the roller keeps coming back over so the old cuts silt up and the whole image is cut again from underneath.

energy.doc: how fast the cutter works, how hard the light rakes the form, and the wet-ink sheen

density.doc: how loaded the roller is — ink haze and squash across the sheet, plus gouge width and length

speed.doc: rate multiplier on cutting, re-inking and the drift of the form

scale.doc: size of the forms the cutter is chasing

hue.doc: ink hue — 28 is a warm block black; carries the stock and the tone block with it

x.doc: where the light comes from, x

y.doc: where the light comes from, y

act.doc: multi-minute program: steady cutting / the block is opened right up then closes back in / a light hand, mostly ink

style.doc: aesthetic: plank-grain black with knots printing through / clean wide-gouge lino in deep blue-black on grey stock / two-block tonal woodcut, an ochre tone block under the key / red-ochre chalk ink on toned stock / end-grain wood engraving — form built from thin white lines cut into a solid black field

seed.doc: deterministic block — grain direction, knots, gouge character, stock fibre
